dossier_meta.catalog_title: r-regular graphs are not uniquely hamiltonian.
dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Basic Graph Theory » Cycles
dossier_meta.statement_text: Conjecture If $ G $ is a finite $ r $ -regular graph, where $ r > 2 $ , then $ G $ is not uniquely hamiltonian.
dossier_meta.context_text: (Reproduced from [M].) A graph $ G $ is said to be uniquely hamiltonian if it contains precisely one Hamiltonian cycle . This conjecture has been proved for all odd values of $ r $ [T] and for all even values of $ r > 23 $ [H]. By Petersen's theorem, it would suffice to prove it for $ r = 4 $ .
